judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass House Bill 5024. Government and federal immigration detention centers cannot operate or be built within 1,500 feet of a school, day care, cemetery, park, forest preserve, public housing, home, or place of worship, whatever address they use. The Illinois Senate passed it 39-17, and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to accept the House version of Senate Bill 2437. It requires doula access within six months and covers certain foreign-born crime victims, pregnancy choline, mental-health drug reports, and certified family caregivers for nursing-type work. The Senate had passed a doula-only version 56-0 in April; it accepted this larger Medicaid package 36-19, and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted yes to accept the Senate's rewrite of House Bill 5090. The Illinois House agreed 83-28 and the bill became law as Public Act 104-0788. On the session's last night the Senate deleted the bill's construction-purchasing text. It put a rideshare labor act in its place. That law lets rideshare drivers organize and bargain as a group with the companies. The state labor board must certify one group to speak for all covered drivers. Covered companies must bargain with that group and follow new unfair-practice rules. Each rideshare trip starting in Illinois now carries a fee paid into a new driver support fund. The House had passed the earlier construction version 101-1 in April 2026.

Covered companies must bargain with that group and follow new unfair-practice rules. Each rideshare trip starting in Illinois now carries a fee paid into a new driver support fund. The House had passed the earlier construction version 101-1 in April 2026.
